ai_text_001.text: Solutions to mitigate UHI include increasing urban greenery, implementing reflective roofing materials, and using permeable pavements to reduce heat absorption and enhance cooling.

ai_text_002.text: Cool Roofs reflect sunlight and reduce heat absorption, making them ideal for desert cities with intense solar radiation. Green Roofs provide insulation and evapotranspiration, better suited for tropical cities with higher humidity and rainfall.
ai_text_002.summary: Cool vs Green Roofs for climates

ai_text_003.text: Planting urban trees and creating vertical gardens can enhance evapotranspiration, reducing the Urban Heat Island effect while improving air quality and aesthetics.

ai_next_001.text: Comparing Cool Roofs and Green Roofs: - Cool Roofs: Reflect sunlight, reducing heat absorption; ideal for hot, dry climates. - Green Roofs: Provide insulation and evapotranspiration; better for humid, tropical areas.

ai_text_004.text: Physics Fundamentals: - Albedo: Reflectivity of surfaces; impacts heat absorption. - Thermal Mass: Material's ability to store and release heat. - Evapotranspiration: Cooling through water vapor release by plants.

ai_text_005.text: Micro-Climate Intervention Proposal: - Use reflective coatings on building facades to increase Albedo. - Replace asphalt with permeable pavements to reduce heat retention. - Install small vertical gardens on walls to enhance evapotranspiration.

ai_text_006.text: Urban Heat Island mitigation strategies should prioritize solutions like reflective surfaces, permeable pavements, and urban greenery to balance cooling and sustainability.
